summary: The round-3 hardening of the interactive-session write gate genuinely closes the three bugs it claims to (config-file/env-var cgroup override, missing leading '+' strip, single-refspec-only checking), and the dual INVOCATION_ID+kernel-cgroup signal plus PATH-based wrapper-script mechanism is a sound design that correctly defeats the `command` builtin bypass from round 2; the accompanying tests genuinely source and exercise the real shipped snippet rather than a reimplementation. However, both wrapper scripts detect the dangerous subcommand by checking only a fixed argument position -- `git`'s wrapper only checks `[ "$1" = "push" ]` and `gh`'s only checks `[ "$1" = "pr" ] && [ "$2" = "merge" ]` -- which misses the extremely common case of global flags preceding the subcommand: `git -C <path> push origin master` (or `-c`, `--git-dir=`, `--work-tree=`, etc.) leaves $1 as the flag, not "push", and `gh --repo owner/repo pr merge 123 --merge` (gh's -R/--repo is a documented global flag usable before the subcommand) leaves $1 as "--repo", not "pr" -- both sail straight through to the real binary completely unblocked. Unlike the two limitations this round honestly discloses (absolute-path invocation, `command -p`), which require an operator to deliberately go find a real binary path, these are ordinary invocation styles used constantly in scripts and by habit, so the guard can silently fail to engage during unremarkable interactive use, not just deliberate circumvention -- the same bug class (checking only a fixed argument position) that rounds 1-3 each found and closed elsewhere, recurring here undetected and undisclosed. No .github/workflows/** files are touched by this diff.
issues: git wrapper only checks $1 == "push"; any git global option before the subcommand (git -C <dir> push origin master, git -c x=y push origin master, git --git-dir=... push origin master) bypasses branch-protection detection entirely and reaches the real git unblocked.

gh wrapper only checks $1/$2 == "pr"/"merge"; gh's global -R/--repo flag placed before the subcommand (gh --repo owner/repo pr merge 123 --merge) bypasses merge detection entirely and reaches the real gh unblocked.
Neither gap is listed in the article's or snippet's known_limitations section, so the documented threat model overstates what is actually closed.
